newsitem.title: GERMANY: Pro Sieben set for Monday share listing.
newsitem.headline: Pro Sieben set for Monday share listing.

text.p: Pro Sieben AG, whose public offering was 50 times oversubscribed, is set to become the first German television broadcaster to list its shares on the stock market on Monday.

The price for the new preference shares was set on Saturday at 72 marks, but the shares have already been trading in the grey market at nearly 120 marks and Pro Sieben said only one in 10 bidders will receive any shares at all.
The issue price was at the top of the range announced last week at the end of the 10-day book-building period.
The issue will raise 1.26 billion marks for the company, and increase its capital by 360 million marks to over 700 million marks.
The company scheduled a news conference for 0830 GMT on Monday to give further details of the issue.
The issue is being managed by a banking consortium led by BHF-Bank AG, Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG, and Salomon Brothers.

A total 850 million shares were ordered though only 17.5 million will go on the market. 52.5 percent of the issue will be placed with German individual investors. Thirty-three percent of the orders came from outside Germany.
Pro Sieben chief executive Georg Kofler said, "The high demand makes the issue one of the most successful in German stock-market history."
Pro Sieben network's market share in June rose to 9.6 percent, up about half a point, while its Kabel 1 network's market share was steady at four percent.

Due to the high degree of oversubscription, the company said a complex lottery would be used to fill the orders. Only one subscriber in ten will receive any shares at all, and even winners will get only a portion of the shares they ordered.
"In the allotment, equal opportunity was our highest principle," Kofler said.
The company is also restructuring its shareholder structure to make Thomas Kirch, son of Bavarian media mogul Leo Kirch, its majority shareholder with 60 percent of the ordinary voting shares.
Retail group Rewe holds the remaining 40 percent.
Kofler has said in the past the company plans to issue ordinary shares to the market before the year 2000.
